title: Ankhorage Chess
summary: Provides a framework-independent headless rules engine for configurable chess boards.
purpose: Give applications reusable chess rules and state transitions without coupling game logic to rendering or a framework.
responsibilities: Define configurable chess-board and game-state types.
Create a headless chess engine for legal moves and game results.
boundaries: Does not render a chess board or own a user interface.
Does not provide multiplayer transport or persistence.
Does not require a framework or hosting provider.
audience: Application authors building configurable chess experiences.
useCases: Validate and apply chess moves through a headless engine.
Model configurable chess boards and game states.

invariants: Rules and state transitions remain independent of rendering and transport.
Consumers own persistence and multiplayer coordination.

limitations: UI, persistence, and network play are outside the engine.
